commands_run: bash run_in_docker.sh "mvn -q -B -DskipTests compile && mkdir -p .security-pipeline/pov/classes && javac -cp target/classes -d .security-pipeline/pov/classes .security-pipeline/pov/CommandInjectionPov.java && java -cp target/classes:.security-pipeline/pov/classes CommandInjectionPov"
output_json.diff_review: Diff is scoped and minimal: BourneShell.java switches the executable quote delimiter from '"' to '\'' and enables single-quote escaping (mirroring the already-safe argument handling), removes the unsafe getExecutable() override that pre-quoted via unifyQuotes()/double-quotes, and adds '"' to the quoting trigger chars. Shell.java adds an executableEscapePattern field/accessor and swaps the hardcoded '\\' escape char for the String-based escape-pattern overload of StringUtils.quoteAndEscape — this exactly mirrors the overload already used for arguments (getArgumentEscapePattern()), so it's not a novel/risky code path. Test-only changes add BourneShellTest cases for $(...), backtick, semicolon, embedded-single-quote, and no-metachar executables, plus a CommandlineTest end-to-end execution test. No unrelated behavior changes; CmdShell/Windows and argument-quoting opt-out are left untouched with justification. The diff itself is well-reasoned and directionally correct — the flaw is that it doesn't go far enough: it swaps one quoting scheme for another that shares the same underlying quoteAndEscape short-circuit weakness, without addressing that weakness (e.g. by not relying on startsWith/endsWith shortcut when quoting untrusted raw input, or by rejecting/escaping unbalanced or unexpected quote sequences).
issues: Live CWE-078 bypass: Commandline#setExecutable("'true'; touch <marker>; echo ''") still achieves arbitrary command execution after the patch, because StringUtils.quoteAndEscape's startsWith/endsWith 'already quoted' short-circuit causes the raw (attacker-controlled) executable string to be emitted completely unescaped and unquoted whenever it happens to start and end with the new single-quote delimiter.

The patcher's own regression_hint/exploiter notes explicitly flagged this exact bypass class ('bypassing the already quoted short-circuit in quoteAndEscape's startsWith/endsWith check') as required coverage, but no test for it was added for the executable path, so the gap went undetected.
output_json.pov_result: Reran the provided PoV independently via the Docker wrapper against the patched worktree: `Shell command line: [/bin/sh, -c, 'true$(touch /tmp/plexus_pov_marker....txt)']` followed by `NOT VULNERABLE: injected shell command did not execute`, exit code 1 — confirms the original PoV no longer reproduces. However, I additionally crafted a new PoV (BypassCheck2.java, not part of the delivered patch) using executable = `'true'; touch <marker>; echo ''` (a balanced-quote string that both starts and ends with `'`). Running it against the same patched worktree produced: `Shell command line: [/bin/sh, -c, 'true'; touch /tmp/plexus_bypass2_marker....txt; echo '']` followed by `BYPASS CONFIRMED: injected shell command executed; marker created at ...`. This demonstrates the same CWE-078 command-injection impact survives the patch via a different executable string, exploiting quoteAndEscape's "already quoted" short-circuit which returns the source completely unescaped when it happens to start and end with the quote delimiter character.
output_json.regression_result: All regression commands pass when rerun independently in the Docker container: `mvn -B -DskipTests package` succeeds; `mvn -B test` runs 289 tests with 0 failures/0 errors (including the new BourneShellTest and CommandlineTest cases). Regression suite is green, but this does not offset the confirmed security bypass since none of the new tests exercise a balanced-quote/short-circuit payload.
output_json.summary: The patch correctly fixes the original PoV (command substitution in Commandline#setExecutable no longer executes) and all regression tests pass, but the fix is incomplete: it reuses StringUtils.quoteAndEscape's pre-existing "already quoted" short-circuit (source.startsWith(quoteChar) && source.endsWith(quoteChar) -> return source unescaped) for the executable's new single-quote delimiter. I independently crafted and verified a balanced-quote payload (`'true'; touch <marker>; echo ''`) that starts and ends with `'`, triggers that short-circuit, skips all escaping, and results in the injected `touch` command actually executing via /bin/sh -c — reproducing the exact same CWE-078 impact the patch was meant to close, through the same Commandline#setExecutable(String) entry point. This is precisely the bypass class the exploiter's own regression_hint warned about ("bypassing the 'already quoted' short-circuit in quoteAndEscape's startsWith/endsWith check") and it was not covered by the patcher's new tests, all of which use payloads that don't start AND end with a single quote.
